channel.title: Tredyffrin Township, Chester County, PA — Meeting Digest
channel.description: Plain-language digests of Tredyffrin Township, Chester County, PA Board of Supervisors meetings, generated from official public minutes. Unofficial, not affiliated with the township.

item.title: Board of Supervisors — 2026-10-05
item.description:
• Body camera contract renewed through 2031. The board unanimously approved a five-year renewal with Axon Enterprises for police body-worn cameras, starting in 2027: $80,254.91 in October 2027 (no increase over 2026), then $78,641.90 a year from 2028 through 2031. The cost is already budgeted and prices are locked in for five years. A resident raised concerns about an automated report-writing feature that comes with the product; police said the department isn't using it.
  • Traffic software with privacy questions. The board unanimously approved a three-year contract with Urban SDK for traffic management software, $23,850 a year starting January 2027. Mr. Bhaskar raised privacy concerns and said IT and the vendor assured him the data can't be tied to individuals; police said no license plate or personal data will be collected, and PDF copies of complaints will be viewable online. Onboarding begins before January 1.
  • Charter referendum awareness. A resident worried that voters don't know about the November ballot referendum on updates to the Township Home Rule Charter. Staff listed their outreach: open houses, a website banner, social media, lobby postings, the printed newsletter and the e-newsletter. Supervisors committed to an executive overview at the October 19 meeting. Ms. Johnston-Pugh noted the open houses were poorly attended and pointed to a red-lined version of the changes on the township website, and Mr. van Mol said the ballot wording was written by Chester County Voter Services from township information.
  • Open space grant. The board adopted Resolution 2026-16, 7–0, authorizing an application to the 2026 PECO Green Region Open Space Program for the Airdrie Preserve project.
  • Winter salt costs more. The board approved the 2026–2027 salt contract with the lowest qualified bidder, Chemical Equipment Labs, at $78.90 a ton, up $7.73 from last year. Asked about reserves, staff said there are none left from last year.
  • Employee dress code updated. The board unanimously approved updates to the Employee Dress Code Policy. The chief operating officer said many of the revisions were to use gender-neutral language.
  • Deer overpopulation. Ms. Humble raised a letter about deer overpopulation. Dr. Gosse said the township works with two deer management groups for culling but is limited in where they can work.
  • Public access to meetings. A resident asked why not every authority, board and commission meeting is on Zoom. Staff said the township can't broadcast all of them: Board of Supervisors meetings are the only ones televised, and those and the Fire Commission's are the only ones on Zoom. The same resident said some board and commission minutes are missing from the website and asked for faster posting.
  • Dates coming up. A conditional use hearing for Chabad Lubavitch of Chester County & Western Main Line is Oct 19 at 5:30 PM. The Fire Commission's 2027 preliminary budget workshop is Oct 7 at 6 PM in Keene Hall, and the Arts Commission's fall art show reception is Oct 9, 5–7 PM at the Township Building. The board also proclaimed Oct 4–10 Fire Prevention Week, 7–0. Township offices close Oct 12.

item.title: Board of Supervisors — 2026-09-21
item.description:
• Student rental ordinance adopted. After a public hearing, the board voted 7–0 to adopt Ordinance HR-499, which deletes and replaces Chapter 151, Property Registration for Student Homes. The minutes don't summarize the hearing testimony.
  • Earned income tax motion died for lack of a second. Mr. Bhaskar moved to direct staff to work with the solicitor on implementing an Earned Income Tax (EIT) paired with a real estate tax rollback, and described who would be affected. No supervisor seconded it, so it did not pass. Four residents spoke on the idea during public comment: one raised concerns, one said businesses locate in Tredyffrin partly because it has no EIT, one asked for more detail if the issue returns, and one criticized how the crowd treated the supervisors and asked them to look for ways to cut expenses.
  • Sewer capacity project. The board authorized submitting Pact Two's proposal for the Devon Park Drive / 501 Swedesford Road sanitary sewer capacity enhancement project at $1,300,000, and approved a sewer agreement with 435 Devon Park Partners LLC. It also approved $25,955.25 to rebuild a pump at the Chesterbrook Pump Station.
  • West Circular Avenue stormwater push. The board approved Jacobs for engineering design at $280,000 for the West Circular Avenue / Spring Street stormwater and drainage project, and authorized staff to apply for a $2,900,000 PennDOT MTF grant, with a letter of support and financial commitment. Asked what happens if the grant is denied, staff said other grant sources exist.
  • Friendship Park moves toward bidding. The board approved $29,376.56 in additional design services from Simone Collins and Princeton Hydro and authorized staff to advertise for bids on the park improvements. Work could start by the end of the year. A resident asked why the project isn't going through COSTARS, the state purchasing program.
  • Speed limit hearing set for Oct 19. The board authorized advertising an October 19, 2026 hearing on HR-498, which would amend Chapter 195 (Vehicles and Traffic) to change speed limits, stop intersections, no-parking zones and permit parking zones. A resident supported the changes but said they won't do enough about speeding on Conestoga Road.
  • Two resolutions adopted 7–0. Resolution 2026-15 adopts the Chester County Hazard Mitigation Plan as Tredyffrin's official plan. Resolution 2026-16 urges the Pennsylvania General Assembly to enact Extreme Risk Protection Orders (ERPO); Police Chief Beaty expressed support.
  • Other approvals. Audit: staff may issue an RFP for financial statement audits. Pensions: 2027 Minimum Municipal Obligations for the police and non-uniformed plans. Buildings: $18,043 for HVAC repairs at 1485 Valley Forge Road (a fire company official asked about mold; staff said remediation is underway). Vehicles: sale of four used township vehicles and a trade-in of a 2015 Ford Escape. Also a settlement agreement with Hunt Engineering and Brown and Caldwell, a lot line change for 920, 958 and 966 North Valley Forge Road, and a final $24,407.58 escrow release for 105 Vincent.
  • Appointments and recognition. Kate Hunsberger joins the Park & Recreation Board; Rob Croner and Kristin Dormuth were reappointed to the Libraries Board of Trustees; Jeff DuVouno of Brandywine Realty Trust joins the Comprehensive Plan Subcommittee. Corporal Chris Middleton was promoted to Sergeant and received an Award of Merit for a serious incident in August.
  • Process and other comments. Mr. Miller proposed requiring two cosponsors before an item goes on the agenda, and Dr. Gosse added that items should first go through the relevant committee. The Park & Recreation Board chair urged the supervisors to manage meetings better, possibly under Robert's Rules of Order. A resident asked whether an ordinance on data centers is planned, and was told the supervisors are considering the issue. The next meeting is October 5.

item.title: Board of Supervisors — 2026-08-17
item.description:
• Rental upkeep concerns raised. A resident shared concerns about rental properties in Chesterbrook, saying landlords aren't maintaining them to the same standard as neighboring homeowner-occupied properties.
  • Student rental ordinance hearing set. The board voted unanimously to advertise a September 21, 2026 public hearing on HR-499, which would replace Chapter 151 on property registration for student homes, putting enforcement responsibility on landlords.
  • Wilson Farm Park change orders approved. The board unanimously approved soil remediation change orders and a General Recreation invoice totaling $483,344.93 for the Wilson Farm Park Tot Lot project.
  • Comprehensive Plan working group created. The board unanimously approved forming a working group - staff, supervisors, planning commission members, an environmental council member, and community stakeholders - to update the township's comprehensive plan.
  • Gregory Lane stormwater project awarded. The board unanimously approved Associated Paving Contractors, Inc. as the lowest qualified bidder for the Gregory Lane Phase 2 stormwater project with Jenkins Arboretum, at a cost of $173,970.
  • Footbridge demolition concerns raised. Multiple Chesterbrook residents voiced opposition to Picket Post Swim Club's planned demolition of a pedestrian footbridge near Bradford Road and asked supervisors to intervene; Mr. Miller said the township is organizing a meeting to discuss the issue.
  • Home Rule Charter information requested. A resident asked how information about the Home Rule Charter Amendment on the November ballot would be shared; Mr. Miller said the township will use its website, social media, and e-newsletter to educate voters.

item.title: Board of Supervisors — 2026-07-20
item.description:
• Property acquired. The board voted 6-0 to adopt Ordinance HR-497, approving the township's acquisition of property at 599 Park Ridge Drive.
  • Split vote on a park event. A proposal for an "America 250 Reenactment Camp" in Teegarden Park (Sept 19-20, $3,000) passed 4-2, with dissenters citing Park & Recreation Board concerns about overnight camping, safety, and lease complications.
  • Road & sewer work approved. $187,745 for stormwater relining on Upper Weadley Road, plus a $21,069.68 emergency sewer repair on Pugh Road.
  • A retirement, recognized. Officer Joseph Butler was honored for 24+ years of police service; volunteer Stanford Nishikawa was also recognized.
  • Residents pushed back again. Concerns were raised about Wilson Farm Park renovation costs, and about the Chase Road Park project's accelerated timeline and rising expenses.

item.title: Board of Supervisors — 2026-06-15
item.description:
• Chase Road Park hits a snag. A resident asked the board to "pause the project and reconsider the costs and scope." The board voted 5-2 to postpone the Change Order #1 decision to the July 20 meeting.
  • Big equipment purchase. A new street sweeper was approved for $337,594.
  • Utility work. A pump station connection installation was approved for $29,800, and $64,565.80 in escrow was released for the Berwyn Village development.
  • Recordkeeping. An addition was made to the township's Historic Resources Map.
  • Housekeeping. Offices announced closures for Juneteenth and July 2-3 for Independence Day; the Chester County Planning Commission presented the township with an official America250PA Chester County flag.

item.title: Board of Supervisors — 2026-05-20
item.description:
• Chase Road Park kicks off. The board awarded a $1.77 million contract for Chase Road Park upgrades - the project that would draw resident pushback the following month.
  • Charter change adopted. Following a public hearing, the board voted 6-0 to adopt Ordinance HR-496, amending the Township's Home Rule Charter.
  • Major projects greenlit. $1.17 million for 2026 road paving (Superpave), a $1.33 million TASA grant for Valley Forge Road pedestrian/sidewalk improvements, $24,370 for emergency culvert repairs, and a $147,200 design contract for sanitary sewer main upgrades.
  • Appointments. Michele Burger joined the Park & Recreation Board; Mark Dixon and Pearl Nudy were reappointed to the Historical Commission; Kim Tempas joined the Environmental Advisory Council.
  • Recognitions. Sergeant Kevin Moore was honored for 46 years of police service; Officer Brittany Rosenfeld received Officer of the Year.
  • Student housing concerns. Residents raised issues about student housing in the Mt. Pleasant neighborhood; supervisors committed to working with Villanova University and updating enforcement ordinances.

item.title: Board of Supervisors — 2026-04-20
item.description:
• Charter amendment adopted. Following a public hearing, the board voted 7-0 to adopt Ordinance HR-495 amending the Home Rule Charter's Chapter 4 governance provisions, and scheduled a May 20 public hearing for a related amendment, Ordinance HR-496.
  • Mental health and policing. A resident pushed for Pennsylvania "red flag" laws and raised concerns about police response to mental health crises; another resident asked the board to consider adding a mental health specialist to police staff.
  • Data centers on the table. The board authorized staff to begin drafting zoning amendments specifically for data centers, after a resident urged including solar and other ecological requirements.
  • Capital spending. $54,600 for a sanitary sewer pump at the Chesterbrook Pump Station, plus $29,717 for surface-cleaning equipment and $24,056.40 for accessible door hardware at the library.
  • Library milestone. Friends of the Tredyffrin Library presented Library Director Mallory Hoffman with a $44,500 check; Township Engineer Stephen Burgo won a Valley Forge Trout Unlimited award for stormwater and environmental work.
  • Traffic concerns raised. Residents flagged speeding on Upper Gulph and King of Prussia Roads, plus traffic and student-housing issues in the Mt. Pleasant and Panhandle neighborhoods.

item.title: Board of Supervisors — 2026-03-16
item.description:
• Residents pressed for answers. The board addressed a March 7 incident at Contention Lane and Old State Road; a resident requested "a follow up public forum" after residents raised concerns about communication gaps.
  • Water rescue equipment funded. $25,293.55 was approved for new water rescue equipment for the Tredyffrin-Easttown Fire Department.
  • Flood buyout grant. The board approved a Hazard Mitigation Grant Program application to acquire a flood-plain home on Yellow Springs Road.
  • Mill Road Park bathrooms. $140,000 was approved for a new bathroom facility, funded by grants.
  • Charter amendments teed up. The board scheduled an April 20 public hearing for Ordinance HR-495, while postponing a related ordinance, HR-496, for further review.
  • Also approved. The 2025 Subdivision & Land Development Activities Report (unanimous), alcohol service at three library fundraising events, and a resolution marking National Libraries Week (7-0).

item.title: Board of Supervisors — 2026-03-02
item.description:
• A federal office lease drew a crowd. The township issued a statement on the Department of Homeland Security leasing space at 1000 West Lakes; six residents spoke against it over concerns about ICE activity, and the township solicitor noted Chester County's position that local police won't assist ICE except for public-safety matters.
  • Gun range and equipment. $199,255 approved for police gun range improvements, plus $30,735 for three new copiers and $58,455 for storm inlet tops.
  • Leaf blowers raised. Residents asked the board to consider an ordinance banning gas-powered leaf blowers.
  • Chase Road Park idea shelved. A resident-proposed community garden at 355 Chase Road was discussed but dropped for lack of support.
  • Other approvals. $9,800 for Friendship Park permitting, $13,121.92 for a sewer root-control program, and a resolution marking April as "PA 811 Safe Digging Month" (7-0).
  • Recognitions. Township Manager William Martin received a 35-year service award from ICMA; NovoCure and Metropolitan Veterinary Associates were recognized as Gold Level Sponsors of parks programming.

item.title: Board of Supervisors — 2026-02-02
item.description:
• Police fleet expansion. The board approved $212,473 for four new police vehicles (one Tahoe, three Ford Interceptors) plus $77,527 in upfit costs, a separate $34,071.02 utility vehicle, and a $13,500 police drone - all unanimous.
  • Camera and tech upgrades. $42,379 for camera system upgrades at the Police Department, Township Building, and Paoli Library; $28,000 for new sewer/stormwater monitoring software; and up to $50,000 for phase 2 of records digitization.
  • Fire station heating swap. $133,000 was approved to convert the Fire Company substation on Valley Grove Road from oil to gas heat.
  • Environmental grants. The board backed a $100,000 Trout Unlimited grant application for Valley Creek restoration, and reallocated Bike Park Grant funds toward the Chase Road Park project.
  • Wilson Farm Park safety fix. A $12,745 change order was approved to bring the park's tot lot gates up to safety code.
  • Residents pushed back. Two residents questioned the pace of capital spending; several residents raised stormwater concerns tied to a proposed development at 317 Greene Street; and one resident argued Chase Road Park should prioritize children's equipment over pickleball courts.
